# Archive: Workstreams C and D, superseded by the Log & Location rework split

**Date:** 2026-08-24
**Why this file exists:** `docs/plans/pr26-rework.md`'s Workstreams C and D are being replaced by
a six-piece split (L1–L6), recorded in that file's current state. Per this directory's own
convention, the superseded content is archived verbatim here rather than silently overwritten —
a later reader asking "what did C used to mean" should find an answer, not a dead end.

**Status:** point-in-time record as of the date above. Do not edit this file to reflect later
fixes or further plan changes — write a new dated file instead.

---

## Workstream C and D, verbatim, as they stood in `docs/plans/pr26-rework.md` before this rewrite

### Workstream C — Delete-block flow

> **Depends on:** A (the FK) and B (the composable and the interface).
>
> WS5's UI half. Two-step delete-block: when a region has referencing log entries, name them and
> require explicit confirmation, extending `OfflineRegionsSection`'s `pendingDeleteRegion`.
> Delete-block logic in `AvailabilityViewModel.kt`.
>
> **Design constraint from #26's own design doc:** do not promise a specific reclaimed amount on
> delete. Sizes don't sum to disk usage (tiles are shared/dedup'd), and deleting one of two
> overlapping regions frees much less than its reported size.
>
> **Gate:** compile + tests green; the two-step flow exercised in a Compose test.

### Workstream D — Entry-level tile capture

> **Depends on:** A and C.
>
> A ~1m-radius `download()` call per referencing entry, triggered only after C's delete-block
> confirmation, blocking the region delete on any capture failure. New user-facing string in
> `strings.xml`, matching the existing state-phrased register (`track_recording_needs_location`
> is the model).
>
> **Note:** this workstream's original text called `download(name, region, onProgress)`
> "unchanged." That is true only after B lands — against `main`'s current signature it is a
> breaking reference.
>
> **Gate:** compile + tests green; capture failure demonstrably blocks the delete.

---

## Why superseded

**C's actual deliverable shipped early, inside Workstream B, before C was ever dispatched.** B
ported PR #26's `OfflineRegionsSection` composable wholesale, including its delete-confirmation
`AlertDialog` (`pendingDeleteRegion`, "Delete "..."?" / Delete / Cancel) — the exact UI C was
scoped to build. Verified directly against shipped source during a read-only scoping pulse
(2026-08-22), not assumed: `AvailabilityScreen.kt`'s `OfflineRegionsSection` already has this
dialog, landed under Workstream B's commit, before any C dispatch existed.

Separately, the owner changed the underlying design (2026-08-22): tile capture no longer happens
at region-delete time at all, so C's original purpose — blocking a delete that would strand a
referencing entry's tile — describes a risk that no longer exists. Under the new design nothing
is at risk during a delete, because deletion was never the capture trigger to begin with.

**D's trigger moved from delete-time to location-set.** D was scoped to capture a ~1m tile per
referencing entry *at the moment a region was about to be deleted* — the last chance to preserve
what an entry pointed at. The owner's reasoning for changing this (2026-08-22): **capture-on-delete
makes an entry's own journal tile contingent on a moment that may never come, or may come with no
signal at all** — an entry that's never involved in a region delete would simply never get a tile,
silently, with nothing in the UI ever telling the forager their entry has no offline map backing
it. **Capture-on-location-set makes each entry self-sufficient from the start**: the tile is tied
to the one piece of information every located entry already has — where it is — rather than to an
unrelated, possibly-never-triggered lifecycle event on a completely different object (a region).

## The rework grew beyond the offline feature

While reworking when capture happens, the owner chose to also fix two things adjacent to it,
rather than defer them now that the code touching this area is still young and few call sites
depend on it (owner's own framing: interaction patterns and nullable-vs-not decisions are cheap
to change early, expensive once many call sites exist — rework before polish, not after):

- **An interaction change**: every long-press-to-place-a-location gesture in the app (the
  offline-region picker, log-entry creation, waypoint dropping, trip planning) is replaced by a
  single new pattern — a fixed centre pin with the map panned underneath it, confirmed with
  OK/Cancel — rather than shipping the offline-capture feature against the old long-press gesture
  and having to convert it again later once the interaction changed anyway.
- **A domain change**: `MushroomLogEntry.foundAt` becomes optional. Under the new flow, adding an
  entry goes straight to the entry's own page (with Add Location, Camera, and Gallery buttons)
  rather than requiring a location be placed first — so an entry can now exist, briefly or
  indefinitely, with no location at all, which the domain model did not previously allow.

Both changes are recorded as part of the same replacement split (L1–L6) in
`docs/plans/pr26-rework.md`'s current state, not as a second, separate plan — the offline-capture
feature (D's replacement, L6) depends on both landing first (L2, L3), so scoping them together
was necessary, not just convenient.
